subject: Post-demo: assessing private/air-gapped options and maintenance cadence
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Sanders <alex.sanders@genlab.com>, Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@genlab.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: assessing private/air-gapped options and maintenance cadence

Thanks again for your time this morning — appreciate the detailed walkthrough of your compliance constraints. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key notes from the call
- GenLab will likely need a private deployment (VPC or on-prem appliance) to meet data sovereignty and air-gap requirements; hosted API ruled out for regulated workloads in EU/US clinical pipeline.
- Primary question areas: hardware footprint, offline patching/upgrade process, maintenance window and technician access, and procurement lead times.
- Lina will own procurement/ops coordination; Alex will validate security evidence (SOC2, network controls).

Open items (we need answers to qualify sizing and timeline)
1) Expected QPS / typical prompt length distribution for inference (tokens/input). This drives GPU pool sizing and KV cache behavior.
2) On-site spare parts policy — do you have an internal M&O team or will you rely on vendor field techs?
3) Network posture while air-gapped: will systems ever have one-way egress (for monitoring) or fully sealed?
4) Internal change window cadence for firmware/OS patches (monthly/quarterly) and whether we can schedule maintenance windows during off-hours.

Proposed next steps
- I attached a short questionnaire (genlab-private-deploy-questions.xlsx) to capture QPS, data flow, and maintenance preferences. Please fill and return by EOD Friday so we can size a draft BOM.
- If you can share a simple network diagram (masking sensitive IPs) we’ll validate firewall/NAT requirements — I attached a proposed diagram template (proposed-network-diagram.png).
- Marissa (cc’d) will review SLA/fallback options for Dedicated vs Private once we have the inputs; we can set a 30-minute follow-up next week to review the BOM.

Attachments: genlab-private-deploy-questions.xlsx (questions workbook), proposed-network-diagram.png (diagram template)

Thanks — I’ll follow up after I get the filled questionnaire.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Sanders <alex.sanders@genlab.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@genlab.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: assessing private/air-gapped options and maintenance cadence

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side so the questionnaire is accurate: 

Answers / clarifications
- QPS: for the first phase we expect ~8 peak RPS (roughly 60k tokens/min peak) with 95th percentile latency requirement of <250ms for short prompts; longer batch jobs for model fine-tuning are separate and likely scheduled during maintenance windows.
- Air-gap posture: systems are fully sealed; no outbound connectivity allowed from the inference cluster. There is an isolated one-way diodes path for logs but that is managed by our infra team — we will confirm whether that can be used for status heartbeats only.
- On-site spares: we have a small facilities team (~2 people) but expect vendor remote support plus periodic on-site visits for hardware swaps.

Outstanding for us (can you confirm)
- Does Redwood provide an offline upgrade bundle for major runtime updates (signed package) that can be shipped and applied without internet access?
- What is the recommended rollback path if a patch causes model-serving regressions?

We’ll fill the spreadsheet and return by Friday; Lina will send our high-level network diagram (stripped of IPs) by tomorrow.

—Alex
Alex Sanders
VP Engineering, GenLab Therapeutics
alex.sanders@genlab.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Sanders <alex.sanders@genlab.com>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@genlab.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: assessing private/air-gapped options and maintenance cadence

Appreciate the quick answers, Alex — this is exactly what we need to move forward. Quick responses inline below: 

- Offline upgrades: yes. We provide signed offline upgrade bundles for both runtime and model artifacts. The process is: staging -> apply bundle via our offline installer -> smoke tests via supplied test vectors -> approval to commit. We’ll supply a checksum and signed manifest.
- Rollback path: our recommended approach is a blue/green-style model-serving switch. We keep the prior runtime+model artifact cached on the appliance so you can flip back within minutes if regressions appear. We’ll document the exact sequence in the runbook we generate for your deployment.

Next practical steps
- Once you return the questionnaire and the sanitized network diagram, we’ll produce: (a) a draft hardware BOM (GPU count, NVMe sizing, NICs), (b) an offline upgrade playbook, and (c) an ops runbook that includes spare parts list and recommended maintenance cadence.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-min call next Tue 9/7 at 9am PT to review draft BOM. I’ll send a calendar invite once we get confirmation from Lina.

If helpful, Marissa is on this thread to confirm options for SLA tiering and reserved capacity fallback.

Thanks,
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Sanders <alex.sanders@genlab.com>, Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@genlab.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: assessing private/air-gapped options and maintenance cadence

Hi Alex / Lina — looping in a quick note from the Renewals & Solutions side. Two things to keep in mind as you complete the questionnaire: 

1) SLAs & fallback: if you opt for a fully private (on-prem) deployment but want a safety net during major incidents, we can propose a Dedicated capacity fallback (reservation standing by in a cloud region) that your app can failover to for short windows. We’ll include pricing and lead times in the BOM.

2) Procurement cadence: our typical lead time for appliances (from PO to ship) is ~8–10 weeks depending on GPU supply; if you need accelerated fulfillment we can discuss an express procurement add-on. Also, we provide optional SLA for an on-call field technician in the region for quarterly visits.

Ben — please flag any contract redlines we should expect (e.g., acceptance criteria, security audit windows) so Alex/Lina can align with their procurement team.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
